title: Kernel kickoff diary - daily triage and quick wins
content:
Morning kickoff notes (brain dump) - Anika

Context:
- Oncall handoff last night, saw 2 short spikes in 99p latency between 03:20-03:45 UTC. Root cause not obvious in dashboard (no infra autoscale events).
- Customer: small batch image-captioning flow hit higher p90 for ~5 minutes, reported via support (CS-2201).

Quick timeline I have so far:
- 03:18: alert: p99 token latency up by ~180ms on model-quant-xl (subpool-a)
- 03:22: correlating logs show many "kv_cache.miss" events for prefixes that are usually warm
- 03:24: one node (gpu-node-12) shows elevated GPU mem fragmentation metrics in srep
- 03:35: traffic routed away from node-12 by smart-routing, latency returns to baseline by 03:45

Hypotheses:
1) KV cache eviction threshold too aggressive on node-12 after a small spike of cold prefixes -> many tiny prefix recomputations producing token lag.
2) Intermittent fragmentation + small GC-like pauses in the userland runtime causing delayed attention kernel scheduling.
3) Small batch scheduling -> critical path blocking when batching window increased (we increased default max_delay_ms in canary last week).

Immediate triage checklist (what I did / to do):
- [x] Grabbed last 6 hours of router logs: grep for kv_cache.{miss,evict} -> sample paths saved to /tmp/anika/kv-miss-sample.txt
- [x] Pulled srep metrics for node-12 (GPU mem alloc, fragmentation, process RSS) -> attached to the incident thread (link above)
- [ ] Run targeted reproducer for small prefix reruns: use local replay tool with recorded prefix set (replay-run --model quant-xl --seed-prefixes small-prefixes.json)
- [ ] Try lowering max_delay_ms for canary pool back to 3ms from 8ms (rollback plan) and observe p99 for 30m
- [ ] Add temporary metric: kv_cache.eviction_reason (hot/cold/pressure) if we can tag in runtime to get better signals - file a short PR

Quick notes from trying a local reproducer (this morning):
- Reproducer run (seed from 03:15 window) shows repeated recompute at step ~14 in autoreg sequence when cache misses happen; single-threaded run introduces ~120-150ms per recompute.
- Switching to async-kv path in local branch reduces recompute tail by ~60ms (promising), but need to measure memory overhead.

Ideas for short-term mitigations (hours):
- Default reduce canary max_delay_ms to 3ms for all pools (fast rollback available in runtime-config service).
- Add backpressure guard: if node shows >40% fragmentation for 5m, mark pool as degraded and route to standby.
- Increase KV cache soft-cap by 10% for pools with high repeating prefixes (cheap config change).

Notes to self (todo backlog - prioritized):
1) (P0) Instrument eviction_reason in KV cache + push a metric and sample log (ENG-4127) - owner: me - ETA: today EOD.
2) (P0) Repro harness: extend replay-run to toggle async-kv path and collect p99 delta automatically - owner: Diego - ETA: 2026-03-16.
3) (P1) Explore micro-batch scheduling tweak: try fixed-window 2ms vs adaptive (A/B) - owner: Ishaan - ETA: next sprint.
4) (P1) Write short runbook entry for node fragmentation detection + quick remediation steps (route, increase cache, restart worker) - owner: Anika - ETA: 2026-03-14.
5) (P2) Investigate allocator changes that reduced fragmentation in prior runtime release (notes in PR #732) - owner: TBD - ETA: backlogged.

Commands I ran (for future me):
- ssh node-12
- sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -S "2026-03-12 03:00" -U "2026-03-12 04:00" | grep -E "kv_cache|evict|miss" > /tmp/anika/logs-kv-03-12.txt
- ./replay-run --model quant-xl --prefix-file small-prefixes.json --async-kv=off --trace > /tmp/anika/replay-03-12-async-off.log
- curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/runtime-config/pools/canary" -d '{"max_delay_ms":3}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'  (rolled to test canary only)

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Why did only node-12 show fragmentation? Look at kernel driver logs + recent scheduling background jobs on that host.
- Is the recent canary change (max_delay_ms) correlated? Rollback to confirm.
- Do we have sufficient test coverage for frequent-prefix workloads in nightly CI? If not, add a scenario.

Meeting notes (sync w/ Ishaan 10:30):
- Share reproducer outcomes; he will try async-kv path A/B on staging cluster today.
- Diego will sketch metric for eviction_reason and start a tiny PR to add a log tag.
- If reproducer shows >50ms p99 improvement with async-kv, plan a 1-hour brownout test to validate memory impact.

Closing quick wins checklist (I want these done before EOD):
- [ ] Add eviction_reason metric PR (small)
- [ ] Rollback canary max_delay_ms to 3ms on canary only (monitor 30m)
- [ ] Publish short runbook in docs/runtime/runbooks/kv-eviction.md (draft)

Random notes to preserve: 
- Idea: make cache-key sharding aware of model input hash prefixes so that common prefixes cluster to same shard -> reduces cross-shard evictions (longer term perf project).
- Keep a small sample of offending prefixes (top-50) that caused spikes; push to S3 for offline analysis.

End of morning dump.

-- Anika
